targets.title: key commitment verification
targets.property: The derived commit key MUST equal the header's algorithm suite data (commit key), compared in constant time, before any frame is decrypted.

threats.description: Non-committing / mismatched commit key multi-plaintext attack

targets.status: **partly in-crate + model only**. Property (a), the accept/reject **decision** (`esdk/src/message/header.rs`, `suite_data_check`), is verified in-crate — `validate_suite_data` accepts **iff** the header suite data equals the derived commit key **and** the committed length agrees, rejecting commitment-first otherwise; obligation mutation-tested. Property (b), the **ordering** (commitment validation before frame decryption), is now proven **model only** (`verification/commitment_ordering_proofs.rs`) on a model of the decrypt pipeline — same status as VR-002
targets.residual: **not Verus-proven, trusted by design**: (c) *constant time* — the timing of `aws_lc_rs::constant_time::verify_slices_are_equal` is an aws-lc-rs API contract (Verus does not model timing). For (b): the model is **not** a proof about the shipped async `decrypt_steps`; what stays trusted is that `decrypt_steps` is the real pipeline and that the async frame loop runs after the synchronous commitment step returns (an in-place / typestate Stage 2 proof over the shipped path was deliberately not taken). The derived commit key bytes and the comparison FFI stay at the trusted boundary
targets.drift: verification-recommendations.md says `not_started`, but the report gives in_crate, model_only, trusted.

threats.description: Version/content-type downgrade via a bogus byte

targets.status: **in-crate**: big-endian decoding, bounded readers, header-field decisions, the 0x41 Base64 hint (`classify_version_byte`), reserved bytes, IV length, EDK count. **Model only**: the fixed-field header loop and EDK list loop (`io_stream_aligned.rs`)

targets.status: **in-crate**: regular-frame step (`next_expected_frame`), final-frame check (`final_frame_seq_ok`), sequential-run and start-at-1 lemmas
targets.residual: the async loop that threads `expected_frame` (unverified glue)

targets.title: AES-GCM panic freedom
targets.property: AES-GCM encrypt/decrypt never panic for any input; all buffer slicing (cipher_slice, tag append, plaintext gather) is in-bounds.

threats.description: Crafted input causing a crash during crypto

targets.status: **in-crate** (`prim/src/lib.rs`, T2): `aes_encrypt_extend_core` proves the encrypt slice (`cipher_text[old_size..]`) is always in bounds and exactly `message.len()` bytes; `aes_decrypt_len_ok` proves the decrypt plaintext-vs-ciphertext length precondition that rejects an under-sized output buffer before the gather
targets.residual: **not** Verus-proven: the AES-GCM key length (16/24/32) and the IV validity — enforced inside `aws-lc-rs` (`UnboundKey::new` / `Nonce::try_assume_unique_for_key` return `Err`), a trusted boundary; and the crypto itself (aws-lc-rs `seal`/`open`, FFI)
targets.drift: verification-recommendations.md says `model_only_non_ffi`, but the report gives in_crate, trusted.

targets.title: HKDF / key-derivation lengths
targets.property: Key-derivation length checks and output-buffer sizing are total (no panic, no overflow) and accept exactly the lengths the spec allows.
targets.status: **both halves in-crate**. esdk half (`esdk/src/key_derivation.rs`): the V1 identity-KDF key-length check (`identity_kdf_key_len_ok`) and the V2 KDF / message-ID / key-length checks that size the derived encryption key (`check_v2_key_lengths`), total and accept iff the checks pass; `derive_keys` dispatches on the verified `msg_format_version_from_u8`. prim half (`prim/src/hkdf.rs`, T3): the `{16, 24, 32}` key-length decision (`hkdf_key_len_ok`), total and correct against `okm.len()`, and the no-salt slice bound (`salt_size_core` `<= MAX_SALT_SIZE`, `no_salt_slice_core` in bounds)
targets.residual: **prim half trust boundary**: the aws-lc-rs HKDF crypto and the extract/expand/fill results (incl. their `Err`), reached through the adapters outside `verus!`. In esdk, unverified: buffer sizes read directly from MPL getters (V1 output, V2 commit key), the V1 salt table `digest_length`, the `debug_assert!`s

targets.title: data-key non-disclosure
targets.property: During encrypt and decrypt, the plaintext data key and the derived message encryption key are never written directly to the output stream or returned to the caller. They reach the output only through AES-GCM (the message key is its key input) or, for the data key, after the keyring has encrypted it into an EDK. The data key is also the input of the key derivation (HKDF or the identity KDF). The V2 commitment value is derived from the data key but is public by spec: the message header carries it as suite data. It is a declassification, not a leak. Key lengths are public.

threats.description: Plaintext data key leaked (here: through the output stream or a return value)
Key material persists after use (here: handed back to the caller so it outlives the operation)
Malicious keyring — bounds the guarantee: a keyring/CMM receives the key by design, so VR-011 cannot protect against one

targets.status: **confinement** to `esdk/src/secret.rs`, compiler- and clippy-checked (not Verus); **Verus**: the secret types' accessors and the commitment-value declassification
targets.residual: not Verus-proven overall: the encrypt/decrypt flow (plan step 7), the TB-A adapters, aws-lc-rs, keyrings/CMMs and mpl key types are trusted; the PRK hand-off in `key_derivation.rs` is grep-checked only

targets.title: big-endian codec round-trip
targets.property: The verified big-endian encoders and decoders are exact inverses (decode-after-encode is the identity). For every u32 x, if b@ == spec_u32_to_be(x) then spec_be_u32(b) == x as int; for every u64 x, if b@ == spec_u64_to_be(x) then spec_be_u64(b) == x as int. Encoders exist only for u32 and u64, so the round-trip covers those two pairs. u16 has a decoder (be_u16 / spec_be_u16) but no encoder, so there is no u16 round-trip.
targets.status: **in-crate** (`esdk/src/message/serialize_functions.rs`): `lemma_u32_round_trip` and `lemma_u64_round_trip` prove the verified big-endian encoders and decoders are **exact inverses** for `u32` and `u64` — `spec_be_u32(b) == x` when `b@ == spec_u32_to_be(x)`, and the `u64` analogue; mutation-tested. Capability-driven (category 1c), couples the two spec fns each previously verified only against their own side
targets.residual: a functional-correctness lemma about the **codec** only; it says nothing about the async readers/writers (`read_*`/`write_*`) that call the exec helpers. No `u16` round-trip: `u16` has a decoder (`be_u16`) but no encoder. That the exec fns equal std's `from_be_bytes`/`to_be_bytes` rests on their own ensures and the in-module tests, not on these lemmas

targets.title: prim wrapper length contracts (pipeline target VR-2026-C03)
targets.property: The prim wrappers never panic and keep exact length contracts: digest / DigestContext::finish / hmac return Err unless out.len() equals the algorithm's output (tag) length, leave out unchanged on Err, and copy only after the guard; kbkdf_ctr_hmac maps a missing algorithm to its Unavailable error and a derivation failure to its derivation error, with no panic path; generate_random_bytes and constant_time_equal are total.
targets.status: **in-crate** (`prim/src/lib.rs`, `prim/src/ecdsa.rs`): `digest`, `DigestContext::finish` and `hmac` return `Err` unless the buffer has the algorithm's exact length, leave `out` unchanged on `Err`, and copy only after the guard (proven in bounds); `kbkdf_ctr_hmac`'s lookup / error mapping has no panic path; `generate_random_bytes` and `constant_time_equal` are total
targets.residual: **trusted (TCB A1–A13):** the aws-lc-rs output lengths (A2, A5, A8), no-panic of every listed call (incl. the documented `Context::finish` `expect`, F4), and A13 determinism. Not proven: output bytes, constant-time equality semantics and timing. F3: the `Unavailable` branch is dead with aws-lc-rs 1.18.1

targets.title: AES buffer effects (pipeline target VR-2026-C03, BUG-07)
targets.property: aes_encrypt: on a key or nonce Err the caller's buffer is exactly old ++ message; on a seal Err its length is old + |message| with the prefix unchanged; on Ok it is old ++ ct ++ tag (length old + |message| + 16). aes_decrypt, relative to the labeled assumption A-OPEN: Ok implies |plain_text| == |cipher_text|; a buffer longer than the ciphertext passes the prim guard and ends in a callee-side Err.
targets.status: **in-crate** (`prim/src/lib.rs`): BUG-07(a) **proved** — `aes_encrypt` leaves exactly `old ++ message` on a key/nonce `Err`, `old_len + |message|` with prefix unchanged on a seal `Err`, and `old ++ ct ++ tag` (+16) on `Ok`. BUG-07(b) **recorded under A-OPEN** — a decrypt buffer longer than the ciphertext passes the guard and can only end in a callee-side `Err`
targets.residual: **assumed, not proven:** A-OPEN (A20), the 16-byte tag (A19), no-panic of the AES calls. Not proven: crypto, ciphertext/tag bytes, tail bytes after a seal failure. FOLLOW-UP: what the `aes_*` callers do with the buffer after an `Err` (mpl 2 + 2, esdk 2 + 5). BUG-07 itself is not fixed
